meta.purpose: Seed critique pairs for the teaching library (brief, weak draft, strong revision, reasons). Collected 2026-10-23.
meta.quote_policy: quote_status=verbatim means the text was read from the fetched page or local primary text. paraphrase means the fetch returned a description, not the line.

pairs.before: Your Addiction Ends Here
pairs.after: If you think you need rehab, you do.
pairs.defect_named: Brand-voice promise; not the prospect's own inner sentence
pairs.principle: Pull the headline from the prospect's own words (review mining); address the visitor's struggle, not the service's hype
pairs.reason: Wiebe read 500+ Amazon reviews of addiction books and lifted one reviewer's exact sentence (paraphrase of article).

tested.result: >400% more clicks on the CTA, >20% more lead-form submits on next page

pairs.before: Stop Embarrassment
pairs.after: Headline rewritten to add 'your' and replace the pain with the outcome 'wear what you want' (full line in image)
pairs.defect_named: Summarizes a pain instead of describing a tangible one; not visitor-focused
pairs.principle: Be specific; name the outcome the visitor can picture; use 'your'
pairs.reason: Pain-aware/problem-aware visitors respond to relatable, concrete experiences (paraphrase).

tested.result: Variation B: +108% paid conversions (page-level, all changes together)

pairs.before: (generic product subhead)
pairs.after: Added 'just the dab of a towelette'
pairs.defect_named: Visitor cannot picture using the product
pairs.principle: Mechanism made visible in one concrete image
pairs.reason: So visitors can picture using the product (paraphrase).

pairs.before: Order Now (everywhere)
pairs.after: Keep 'Order Now' in header/footer; mid-page buttons become 'Sweat less. Live more.', 'Why suffer? Get SweatBlock now', 'Control your sweat! Order now'
pairs.defect_named: Action-only CTAs for visitors who have not decided
pairs.principle: Calls to value for the undecided; calls to action for the decided
pairs.reason: Measured paid conversions, not clicks, because extra buttons inflate clicks (paraphrase).

pairs.source: Copyhackers, 'great home page copy into killer' (SweatBlock round 2)
pairs.before: Hero that opened on the product (the already-winning control)
pairs.after: excessive sweaters are sweating for all sorts of reasons. It's almost never 'cos it's hot out. ... Excessive sweating makes you feel trapped. [then Brianna testimonial story, then product] + proof '4 million towelettes sold'; 4-step demo removed
pairs.defect_named: Control led with solution for a problem-aware audience
pairs.principle: Lead at the prospect's awareness stage: problem, agitation, then solution; add proof; cut what is not needed to buy
pairs.reason: Lead with a pain the team had heard often; remind readers deodorant does not solve it (paraphrase).

tested.result: +49% (woman hero) and +46% (man hero) paid lift at 99% confidence

pairs.before: Customize the color of your video player appearance.
pairs.after: The Wistia video player defaults to grey. Which is nice. But grey. Why stick with grey when you can go with hot pink... or dollar-bill green... or, well, Wistia Blue?
pairs.defect_named: Reader must imagine what the change looks like
pairs.principle: Specificity reduces the reader's mental work ('Don't make me think')
pairs.reason: Specific version forms images readily (paraphrase).

tested.result: Whole 8-email sequence: +350% paid conversions vs control (HubSpot A/B, Wistia CRO monitored)

pairs.before: 18% is a lot.
pairs.after: Getting 18% more views is pretty major. Videos that used to get 100 views a day now get 118 views a day. In a month, that's an extra 500+ views.
pairs.defect_named: Reader must do the math and may dispute the claim
pairs.principle: Do the math for the reader; dimensionalize numbers
pairs.reason: Removes burden of calculation (paraphrase).

pairs.before: You can add annotations, create calls to action or collect emails through turnstile – all within the video player!
pairs.after: Unpacked into a bullet list, one bullet per feature with what it does for you (bullets in image)
pairs.defect_named: Glosses over the significance of each feature
pairs.principle: One idea per line; unpack stacked features
pairs.reason: Not stated beyond 'Don't make me think'.

pairs.before: Ready to dive into some data?
pairs.after: People are watching your video. Fantastic, right? ... How can you put your new video data to work for you?
pairs.defect_named: A question the prospect may answer 'no' to breaks the persuasion
pairs.principle: Ask only questions that get a yes, or open questions the copy then answers
pairs.reason: First question almost always gets a yes; second requires thought and lets copy guide the answer (paraphrase).

pairs.before: Watch this!
pairs.after: Caption rebuilt from what users say they use Crazy Egg for: 'to validate our design decisions'; headline 'pulled verbatim from a simple, catchy phrase a handful of survey respondents had used'
pairs.defect_named: Marketer's imperative instead of customer's words
pairs.principle: Customer language from surveys/interviews
pairs.reason: Headline and subheads based on top-3 survey answers to 'what was going on in your world...' (paraphrase).

tested.result: Variation D +13% over a CRE-optimized control

pairs.before: Johnson box present
pairs.after: Removed
pairs.defect_named: Occupied high-value space without affecting conversion
pairs.principle: Exclusion test: if removing it is flat, cut it
pairs.reason: Exclusion test showed flat results (paraphrase).

pairs.before: Plans in ascending order, all prices shown
pairs.after: Lead with most expensive; Gold plan price omitted so visitors must click
pairs.defect_named: Cautionary: curiosity clicks that do not convert
pairs.principle: Curiosity moves the click; only a real offer moves the sale
pairs.reason: +927% clicks to Gold but no more Gold sign-ups; Variation 2 better on other goals (paraphrase).

pairs.before: Save one gallon of gas in every ten
pairs.after: Car Owners! Save one gallon of gas in every ten
pairs.defect_named: Audience not called out
pairs.principle: Flag the reader in the headline
pairs.reason: Only change was the headline; same copy (verbatim: 'There was no other change').

pairs.before: RESPOND BY THURSDAY, MAY 19.
pairs.after: RESPOND BY THURSDAY.
pairs.defect_named: Dated deadline reads as distant; undated 'Thursday' reads as this week
pairs.principle: Urgency must feel immediate
pairs.reason: 'computer error' version pulled 39% more (verbatim fragment).

pairs.before: Can You Afford A Dumb Worker?
pairs.after: IQ Test Enclosed (60-second test the office manager gives their photocopier; free gift open and close)
pairs.defect_named: Fear question less involving than a device the reader does
pairs.principle: Involvement device beats a rhetorical threat
pairs.reason: 'the less involving' control (verbatim fragment).

pairs.before: Specific description of the early-bird gift
pairs.after: A Surprise Gift from Me to You...with Love. Everyone loves a surprise gift, especially me! And I've got one for you that's extra special if you respond to my invitation within the next 10 days. ... I can't tell you—that would ruin the surprise! But I can tell you what it's not:
pairs.defect_named: Fully described premium leaves nothing to find out
pairs.principle: A mystery bonus described with tantalizing copy can out-pull a specific one
pairs.reason: 'our strongest early-bird premium proved to be a mystery gift' (verbatim).

tested.result: strongest premium in his Richard Simmons tests; no % given

pairs.before: Free if you reply by January 31.
pairs.after: Free if you reply in 7 days.
pairs.defect_named: Fixed date can already be past when the reader sees it
pairs.principle: Relative deadlines offline; test 10/15/30 days
pairs.reason: Postal/printer delay 'can massacre your response' (verbatim fragment).

pairs.source: Justin Goff reporting David Deutsch critique
pairs.before: Anti-aging email listing buyer pain points (stairs, gardening, grandkids) ending in a promise of renewed energy
pairs.after: Subject: V8 Juice worse for your heart than McDonald's french fries? Body compares V8 sodium to fries, doctors calling V8 'junk'; product pitch only at the end
pairs.defect_named: 'sounded like every other anti-aging email in his inbox' (verbatim as quoted by Goff); 'generic, boiler plate copy'
pairs.principle: A unique hook is the first thing a chief looks for; without it nothing else matters
pairs.reason: Hook sets the email apart, gets it read, pushes to buy (paraphrase).

tested.result: ~$15,400 sales from a $3,500 email drop (not a split test)

pairs.before: Praise-the-product emails like every other affiliate
pairs.after: Subjects: 'The case against Brent Charleton' / 'Is Brent Charleton a SCAM?'; body names the method's real downsides ('even though Brent's method can be uncomfortable...') then endorses
pairs.defect_named: Sameness; nothing forces the open
pairs.principle: Go against the grain; admit the downside to earn belief
pairs.reason: 'went against the grain' so people felt they had to read (paraphrase).

tested.result: all contrarian emails in top 5 of 16 by sales; claimed 3x vs other emails (seller's own numbers)

pairs.source: Justin Goff, offer that flopped vs 320k buyers
pairs.before: Paleo Plenty: 'foodie' recipes of summer salads, zucchini noodles, taro root chips
pairs.after: Paleo Sweets: paleo versions of your favorite brownies, chocolate chip cookies and ice cream
pairs.defect_named: Copy cannot rescue a promise people do not want
pairs.principle: Argument selection precedes writing: pick the desire with mass appeal
pairs.reason: Same price, same format, same $15k copywriter; appeal was the variable (paraphrase).

pairs.source: Kevin Rogers, 'This guy CALLED ME OUT about the sales page'
pairs.before: Letter with proof, testimonials, scarcity, 30-day guarantee
pairs.after: Added a Loom screen-recorded tour of the member area (job forum, critique forum)
pairs.defect_named: Prospect: 'Your sales letter is great. But we can't see what's inside.' (verbatim)
pairs.principle: Show the thing; demonstration beats assertion
pairs.reason: Rogers: 'sometimes the best way to sell something is by simply showing someone exactly what they're buying' (verbatim).

tested.result: the objector bought an annual pass after the video

pairs.before: Copy that 'sound[s] like copy is expected to sound' (verbatim fragment); written in 'writer mode'
pairs.after: No rewrite shown. Fix: write from the part of you that persuades a friend in conversation; picture a person you care about; read it out loud and revise until it does not make you cringe
pairs.defect_named: 'You write well but you rely on that too much.' (verbatim)
pairs.principle: Show there is a person behind the words
pairs.reason: Persuasive instinct comes from conversation, not book reports and memos (paraphrase).

pairs.source: Clayton Makepeace via AWAI, 'Astonishing Power of Fear'
pairs.before: We all know that smoking can kill us – someday in the distant future
pairs.after: No rewrite; rule: make it an imminent fear, close in time and place
pairs.defect_named: Distant consequence loses power
pairs.principle: Fear must be imminent and already waking the prospect at 2:30 AM
pairs.reason: Sugarman's alarm copy works because the break-in is next door (paraphrase).

pairs.before: the entire U.S. economy could come unglued at virtually any moment
pairs.after: No rewrite; narrow to a fear the product can fix (losing money), not collapse
pairs.defect_named: Paralyzing fear freezes instead of moving
pairs.principle: Fear must be actionable by the offer
pairs.reason: 'Using a fear that paralyzes prospects won't do you any good' (verbatim).

pairs.before: Draft whose copy 'sang and soared' but spent many pages on threats; product's answer 'presented quickly and without passion'
pairs.after: Re-balance: fear as short attention-getter, bulk of passion on how the product neutralizes each threat
pairs.defect_named: 'didn't make me want to buy the product' (verbatim)
pairs.principle: 'Nobody buys just because they're afraid.' (verbatim)
pairs.reason: Fear overwhelmed the offer (paraphrase).

pairs.source: Mark Ford via AWAI, 'Ignore this rule...'
pairs.before: The pause that refreshes and always cool
pairs.after: The pause that refreshes
pairs.defect_named: Two ideas; focus lost
pairs.principle: Rule of One: one big idea; other benefits to sidebar or P.S.
pairs.reason: 'the more points you try to cover, the less effective each point' (verbatim, Loftus quoting Ford).

pairs.before: Together we will
pairs.after: No rewrite given
pairs.defect_named: 'doesn't express any benefit for the reader' (verbatim)
pairs.principle: One desirable benefit

pairs.before: Sign up now
pairs.after: Create Your Website
pairs.defect_named: Button names the action, not the value gained
pairs.principle: Button = value, not action
pairs.reason: Value-over-action buttons usually perform better (paraphrase; no test cited).

pairs.before: a better toothbrush
pairs.after: a brighter smile
pairs.defect_named: Sells the product, not what it delivers
pairs.principle: People buy the value delivered

pairs.before: Unlock, unleash, enhance, exceed, empower, supercharge
pairs.after: Words real people say; no replacement list given
pairs.defect_named: 'landing page words' real people do not use
pairs.principle: Write like you talk

pairs.before: Do your taxes faster & better
pairs.after: You'll never again have to worry about how you're going to fit 'doing your taxes' into your busy life.
pairs.defect_named: Broad comparative claim with no situation
pairs.principle: Name the job and the moment the prospect hires the product for
pairs.reason: Swap broad claim for the customer's daily struggle (paraphrase).

pairs.source: Justin Goff, 'does your AI copy sound like a robot'
pairs.before: Get expert guidance, cutting-edge tech, and a supportive community for maximum investment success. ... Don't miss out on achieving financial freedom. Join now!
pairs.after: There's ONE crypto coin that's perfectly positioned to benefit from AI. ... already jumped 237% in the last month ... Sounds crazy, right? ... Ready to see what this 100x coin is?
pairs.defect_named: 'robot speak that means nothing' (verbatim); no curiosity, no emotion, no proof, generic CTA
pairs.principle: Curiosity + proof + specificity + a human voice
pairs.reason: Author sells a prompt bundle; the pair is his demonstration, not a test.

pairs.source: Justin Goff, 'AI turns average copy into A-list copy'
pairs.before: You'll discover how to restore his coat, so he looks young and healthy ... You'll find out how to provide him with flexible and pain-free paws, legs, and hips
pairs.after: Imagine seeing your dog spring off the couch and chase his favorite toy, pain-free and full of boundless energy... There's no more heartache watching him struggle to go up the stairs... No more guilt as you wonder if he's suffering in silence...
pairs.defect_named: 'average, C-level copy' (verbatim): a list of discoveries instead of a scene the owner feels
pairs.principle: Dimensionalize: scene, relief, guilt removed
pairs.reason: 'way more vivid', 'you can feel the emotion' (verbatim). No per-line reasons; AI-produced rewrite.

pairs.before: CTA 'Love at first bite' (link not visibly clickable); reversed-out, centered body copy; low-contrast sales lines
pairs.after: 'See the recipes', underlined; black on white, left-justified
pairs.defect_named: 'isn't the most obvious call to action' (verbatim); 'the invisible sales pitch'
pairs.principle: 'your design must help your copy not hinder it' (verbatim)
pairs.reason: 'Don't make readers' eyes work harder than they need to' (verbatim).

pairs.before: Factual bullet points on the materials, size and function. / A longer description of the maker.
pairs.after: No rewrite; emotional appeal supported by logic; page addresses the buyer's needs, not the maker
pairs.defect_named: Specs alone are 'a conversion slayer' (verbatim); maker-focus is the wrong subject
pairs.principle: Emotion first, logic as support; buyer not maker

pairs.before: Benefits 'in a series of sentences' that are 'difficult to read and comprehend'
pairs.after: List benefits as bullets, each tied to a product feature
pairs.defect_named: Dense sentences hide the benefits
pairs.principle: Scannable bullets linked to features
pairs.reason: Faster to scan, easier to understand, keeps what the writer got right (paraphrase).

review_procedures.url: https://copychief.com/ep-243-new-breed-craig-dave/ (also the show's RSS description at https://copychief.com/feed/podcast/)
review_procedures.status: first-person show notes in Rogers' own feed; unsigned on page
review_procedures.text: In a typical first draft copy review there's something critical on the very first page that needs to be fixed, so I rarely get beyond that before sending over a list of notes.
review_procedures.operational: Review stops at the first page-one failure (usually hook/big idea); notes go back before reading further.

review_procedures.text: Ask: What is the Big Idea here? Is this idea strong enough to capture the hearts of my customers? Are my ideas all over the place? The idea must be easy to grasp immediately, stay consistent throughout, be strong, easy to understand, easy to believe. Writers who list every feature and benefit and throw them all in produce 'B-level' copy.
review_procedures.operational: Five one-things: one idea, one core emotion, one story, one desirable benefit, one inevitable response.

review_procedures.who: Mark Ford via AWAI 'One Big Idea: Tip #1'
review_procedures.text: Name the big idea in one sentence (if you need 'and', there are two). Identify the dominant emotion. Check the lead carries the main benefit. Later benefits must extend the main one, not add new promises. Find skip points: sections only some readers care about give everyone else permission to stop.
review_procedures.operational: Note: the fetch tool invented illustrative examples for this page; none were used.

review_procedures.text: 'Very simply, start with the positive.' Lead with a real strength, 'Don't save it for last', then 'lower the resistance to your suggestions' before raising problems. Goal is 'the best possible copy you can get', not toughening the writer.
review_procedures.operational: Delivery format for the revise step: strength first, then the one change that makes it 'even stronger'.

review_procedures.text: 1 find what shines and say why; 2 check single focus (power of one), flag drift; 3 check benefit presentation; 4 mark reader reactions: the phrases that keep you reading, the section that loses you, the section that moves you to act.
review_procedures.operational: Three reaction marks (kept reading / lost me / moved me) are a usable reviewer output schema.

review_procedures.text: 'Read it out loud.' Revise until it sounds like one half of a real conversation.
review_procedures.operational: Voice test for the AI-failure checklist.

review_procedures.who: Michael Masterson & Mike Palmer, Copy Logic (Agora)
review_procedures.text: Product pages confirm the book teaches 'Mike's simple CUB technique' and 'a four-point copy checklist'. The expansion Confusing/Unbelievable/Boring and the peer-marking procedure are from prior knowledge, not fetched text.
review_procedures.operational: Treat CUB details as medium-confidence until the book is sourced.
